introduction: Oregon weatherization starts with the local agency serving your county. An energy audit determines appropriate work based on the home and available funding.
description: Oregon weatherization starts with the local agency serving your county. An energy audit determines appropriate work based on the home and available funding.

sections.who: Household income and size determine financial eligibility. Priority groups include older adults, people with disabilities and households with children or high energy burdens.
sections.get: Services may include insulation, air-leak reduction, heating improvements, minor energy-related repairs and education.
sections.docs:
• Household income and members.
  • Home address and utility information.
  • Requested ownership or rental permissions.
sections.apply:
1. Contact the county agency

    Use the state weatherization directory.

  2. Complete intake

    Ask for the current checklist and any waiting-list arrangements.

  3. Arrange the energy audit

    Discuss access and required permissions. Review the proposed measures with the provider.
sections.after: Keep provider contact details and ask about any condition preventing work or affecting scheduling.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Weatherization services, priorities and intake. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Can there be a waiting list?
Yes. The state says households may enter a service waiting list after initial contact.
The audit, home condition and funding determine appropriate measures.
The state lists heating-system repair and replacement among possible services.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
